pages.title: Sizes
pages.content:
Sizes

Five household sizes share one building at 48 Alder Row, Lindenport. The way to choose is a free twenty-minute walk with an attendant, then the monthly price of the size that fits.

  • Same-day move-in
    if booked before 15:00
  • Staffed building
    09:00-19:00, 7 days
  • Free hand-truck loan
    $0, no deposit

Three facts sit under the page heading because they apply to every size. Same-day move-in is available when the visit is booked before 15:00, you bring photo ID, and you pay the first month as you sign. The building is staffed from 09:00 to 19:00, seven days, which is what staffed means here. The hand-truck loan is $0, as is the key card and the admin fee, and there is no deposit. Mikura Storage is one dedicated building at 48 Alder Row, Lindenport: six floors, 412 units, and five household sizes. A visit is free, takes about twenty minutes, and comes with no obligation. You walk the corridor with an attendant before you choose.

Five sizes, in order

The names describe a household load, not a second home. Shelf is for a small stack: cartons and a suitcase, the sort of gap a cot or a short move can leave in a small room.

1

Shelf

Shelf is 0.8 m² (9 sq ft). It fits about ten boxes and a suitcase, and the monthly price is $38.

2

Closet

Closet is 1.5 m² (16 sq ft). It fits a wardrobe's worth and a folded bike, at $62 a month.

3

Box Room

Box Room is 3 m² (32 sq ft). It fits a studio flat's contents, at $98 a month.

4

Spare Room

Spare Room is 5 m² (54 sq ft). It fits a one-bedroom flat, at $148 a month.

5

Garage Bay

Garage Bay is 8 m² (86 sq ft). It fits a two-bedroom flat, at $215 a month.

Every unit includes

  • $0Admin fee
  • Climate-held rooms
  • Fire-rated walls
  • Key-card doors
  • 24 h video
  • Free loading bay

Plain monthly prices

Contents cover, optional, all sizes, up to $5,000, for fire, water and theft: $6 a month.

How to measure

Start from the floor area

Start with the square metres you would sign for, not with a feeling that you have "a few things." Shelf is 0.8 m². Closet is 1.5 m². Box Room is 3 m². Spare Room is 5 m². Garage Bay is 8 m². At home, clear a patch of floor to the area you are considering and place the real load inside it: the cartons, the suitcase, the folded bike, the furniture from the flat you are leaving. What stands outside the patch will not fit through good intentions. The attendant can repeat the check here with a tape at an open door during the twenty-minute visit. Measuring is part of the visit. It is not a separate appointment, and it is not billed.

Name the piece that decides it

Most households are sized by the ordinary description. A wardrobe's worth and a folded bike point to Closet. A studio flat's contents point to Box Room. A one-bedroom flat points to Spare Room. A two-bedroom flat points to Garage Bay. Ten boxes and a suitcase point to Shelf. If one object is the reason you are tempted to size up, say so when you book the slot. Mei Lin Ho will look at that object against an open door and say whether it belongs in the size you hoped for or in the next one. A bike that cannot be folded is a different problem from the folded bike in the Closet description. Bring a note of the measurements. The visit is still free if you decide the piece should stay at home.

Leave a path you can walk

A floor filled to the last corner is a floor you cannot use. Households who stay longer than a few weeks, as Hana Yilmaz did for fourteen months in a Closet, or the Okoye family for eight months in a Shelf, need to reach one carton without unloading the rest. Leave a walking gap. Where the unit has shelves, use them so the floor area stays a path rather than a pile. Write down the size you think you need before you come, then change your mind after the walk if the open door says otherwise. The agreement you sign is for one size at its monthly price, for at least one month, with thirty days' notice when you are ready to leave. Nothing in the measuring conversation locks you in before you sign.

Closet is for clothes on a run of wall and a folded bike, or for a long run of books if that is what you actually own. Box Room is the size Owen and Lucia Marsh used between leases, a studio flat's contents kept together. Spare Room takes the contents of a one-bedroom flat. Garage Bay takes a two-bedroom flat and is the largest size we rent to households. Mei Lin Ho, the size adviser, will tell you if a single awkward piece needs the next size up. You can still leave without taking a unit.

The monthly price does not add an admin fee. The admin fee is $0 on every size. The key card is $0. Rooms are climate-held between 18 and 24 C and kept below 60% relative humidity. Walls are fire-rated. Doors open by key card. The building uses 24-hour video. The loading bay is free, and the hand truck is a free loan while you load or collect. Optional contents cover is $6 a month on any size, up to $5,000, for fire, water and theft. These are operating facts. They are not a ranking, and they are not a promise that a particular carton cannot be harmed. Read the cover as optional, with that limit, or decline it.

Book a visit

pages.title: Visit
pages.content:
Visit

A first visit is twenty minutes with an attendant, free, and with no obligation to take a unit. You can still move in the same day when the slot was booked before 15:00.

  • Same-day move-in
    if booked before 15:00
  • Staffed building
    09:00-19:00, 7 days
  • Free hand-truck loan
    $0, no deposit

You can move in the same day if the visit is booked before 15:00, you bring photo ID, and the first month is paid when you sign. The desk is staffed from 09:00 to 19:00, seven days. That is the whole meaning of a staffed building here. A hand truck is yours to borrow at $0 while you load, and the loading bay is free. The key card is $0 and the admin fee is $0. There is no deposit. The visit itself is about twenty minutes, free, and without obligation, with an attendant beside you. Address: 48 Alder Row, Lindenport. Phone: 555-0142. If you would rather wait, you leave with the prices and no agreement.

Three stops in twenty minutes

1

The first minutes at the desk

The twenty minutes begin at the desk, not at a locked door. In the morning Daniel Achebe is head attendant. On weekend days Amara Diallo is at the desk, inside the same 09:00 to 19:00 hours.

2

The corridor, with the door open

From the desk you walk the corridor with the attendant. Closed doors give you the run of the floor. An open door gives you the size.

3

The bay, then the decision

If you are arriving with a car, the covered loading bay is part of the same visit. Rafael Souza looks after the bay and the hand trucks. A couple can unload a hatchback onto a hand truck without a separate booking, and the loan of the truck is $0.

The corridor, with the door open

The attendant can hold a carton while you look in, which is the ordinary picture of a visit here: you see the depth of the room, the shelves if that unit has them, and the path back to the lift. Six floors and 412 units sound large on a page. On the walk they are a single clean corridor and one room you might rent. Mei Lin Ho joins this part when the choice is between two floor areas. You are not timed with a stopwatch, but the visit is planned as twenty minutes so the next household can have the same attention. Questions about climate belong here too: rooms are held between 18 and 24 C and kept below 60% relative humidity.

At the desk

You will see an attendant with a clipboard and a plain record of the slot you booked. Tell them which of the five sizes you think you need, or say that you do not know yet. Priya Nair handles contracts and accounts when the conversation turns into an agreement. No one asks you to sign in the first minute. The building opened in 2014 as one dedicated building, and the desk still treats a first visit as a walk, not as a completed move. If you only wanted to see the corridor, that is a complete visit.

The bay, then the decision

You do not have to unload on the day you look. Many people walk the corridor, go home, and return on a booked move-in. If you do want to start today, the conditions are the ones already stated: booked before 15:00, photo ID, first month paid. You receive a key card for the door. Building access with that card is 06:00 to 23:00, seven days, which is wider than desk hours. After 19:00 the desk is not staffed. The card is how you come and go inside the access window.

Four steps

The visit runs in four steps, side by side, with no extra stage hidden underneath.

1

Book a slot

Book a slot. Use the visit form or call 555-0142 during desk hours.

2

Walk the corridor

Walk the corridor for about twenty minutes with an attendant.

3

Choose and sign

Choose and sign. Signing needs photo ID and the first month.

4

Move in

Move in with the key card and a hand truck.

The minimum term from that signature is one month. When you later leave, the notice is thirty days. Optional contents cover, if you want it, is $6 a month up to $5,000 for fire, water and theft, decided at the desk rather than in the corridor.

Bring with you

Bring six things if you can.

Photo ID, because a signature on the day requires it. Your phone, so the desk can reach you about the slot. Measurements of any piece that might decide the size. A list of what you intend to store, in plain language, so Shelf through Garage Bay can be compared with your actual load. The car plate, if you are coming by car to the loading bay. And a card, so you can pay the first month if you decide to sign.

If you are only walking, the list and the measurements are enough, and the card can stay in your pocket. The visit fee is $0. Nothing on the list is a deposit. There is no deposit on the agreement either.

Bring with you

  • Photo ID
  • Your phone
  • Measurements
  • Your list
  • Car plate
  • A card
Book a visit

pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

Mikura Storage is a household self-storage building founded in 2014 and still run as one address. Ines Varga manages it, with a small crew on the desk, the bay, and the building itself.

1

Founded in 2014

Mikura Storage was founded in 2014 by Ines Varga, who is still the building manager. The work has stayed in one dedicated building at 48 Alder Row, Lindenport. It is household self-storage: the things a city flat cannot hold, kept close enough that you can fetch a carton without planning a journey out of the city.

2

The building

The building is six storeys, with a plain front and a covered loading bay. Inside, corridors run between unit doors. Rooms are held between 18 and 24 C and kept below 60% relative humidity.

3

The crew

Seven people run the building. They are listed as text, in this order.

Founded in 2014

We do not publish awards or rankings, and we do not borrow other companies' names to describe the rooms. The practical facts are the ones on the price list. Five sizes, monthly prices in US dollars, a $0 admin fee, a $0 key card, a $0 hand-truck loan, and no deposit. The minimum term is one month. Notice is thirty days.

Why one building

One building means the same crew covers every unit. There are six floors and 412 units, which is enough for Shelf through Garage Bay without opening a second address. Climate, fire checks, the desk, and the loading bay are all on this site. When you call 555-0142 you reach the desk that can see the corridor, during 09:00 to 19:00, seven days. A key card issued here opens this building from 06:00 to 23:00, seven days, and does not belong to a network of other sites. Ines Varga manages the building she founded rather than a chain of them. If a size is full, the waitlist is for a unit in this building, not for a room we would send you across town to find.

The crew

Seven people run the building.

Ines VargaFounder and building manager

Founded Mikura Storage in 2014 and still manages this building.

Daniel AchebeHead attendant, mornings

Leads the desk on the morning side of the staffed hours.

Mei Lin HoSize adviser

Walks the five floor areas with you and helps you choose.

Rafael SouzaLoading bay and hand trucks

Looks after the covered bay and the trucks you borrow at $0.

Priya NairContracts and accounts

Prepares the agreement and the monthly account.

Jonas WeberBuilding care, climate and fire checks

Looks after the rooms and those checks.

Amara DialloWeekend desk

Staffs the desk on weekend days from 09:00 to 19:00.

A typical day

The building opens to key cards at 06:00. People who already have a card can collect or drop a carton before the desk is staffed. At 09:00 the desk opens. Daniel Achebe leads morning attendants. Visits that were booked run at about twenty minutes each: clipboard, corridor, open door, and a decision.

Mei Lin Ho takes the sizing conversations. Rafael Souza keeps the bay and the hand trucks moving when a household is in the middle of a load. Priya Nair puts the agreement in front of anyone who chooses to sign, checks photo ID, and takes the first month. The desk closes at 19:00. Key-card access continues until 23:00. Weekend days keep the same hours, with Amara Diallo at the desk. That is a full day here. It does not include a night attendant.

Walls are fire-rated. Doors are opened by key card. Video runs 24 hours. None of those sentences says that loss cannot occur. They are the conditions the building is kept to, and Jonas Weber's work is the climate and the fire checks that sit behind them. Households use the building in ordinary ways: a Box Room for five months between leases, a Closet for fourteen months of books, a Shelf for eight months while a cot is folded away. The fourth-floor corridors have been repainted, and that floor is open.

How we keep the building

  • 18-24 C, below 60% humidity
  • Fire-rated walls
  • Key-card doors
  • 24 h video
  • Free loading bay
  • Desk 09:00-19:00

Keeping the building is daily work, not a badge on the door. Jonas Weber carries the climate and fire checks. Rooms stay in the range 18 to 24 C and below 60% relative humidity. Fire-rated walls are part of the building, not an add-on you select at the desk. Key-card doors replace shared keys. Video runs all day and all night. The loading bay stays free to households who are moving in or out, and the hand truck is a loan rather than a hire. The desk is staffed only from 09:00 to 19:00, seven days, including the weekend cover Amara Diallo provides. Outside those hours, access is the card and the 06:00 to 23:00 window, not a promise that an attendant is standing in the corridor.

Book a visit

pages.title: Waitlist
pages.content:
Waitlist

Join the waitlist when the size you need is full. Send an email and the size. The desk writes when a unit of that size is free.

When a size is full

A size can be full even though the building holds 412 units. Shelf, Closet, Box Room, Spare Room, and Garage Bay are separate pools. When the size you need has no open unit, leave an email and the size on this form. You are not asked to pay, to place a deposit, or to take a different size in the meantime. There is no deposit on a unit either, once you do sign. The form comes to Mikura Storage. It is not sent to an outside booking service. We do not publish a waiting time, because we will not invent one. The desk writes when that size has a unit free. Until then, your place on the list is a request, not a reservation and not an agreement.

What to send

The form has two fields that matter: your email, and the size you want. Choose one of the five names. Shelf is $38 a month, Closet is $62, Box Room is $98, Spare Room is $148, and Garage Bay is $215. Contents cover is not a size. If you later want the optional cover, you add it when you sign, at $6 a month, up to $5,000, for fire, water and theft. Do not send a payment to join the list. The first month is paid only when you take a unit, with photo ID, at the desk. If you would rather be shown a smaller or larger room that is free today, book a visit instead. A visit is twenty minutes, free, and without obligation.

After you send the form

You will see a short confirmation on the site. During desk hours, 09:00 to 19:00, seven days, the desk can also take the same request by phone on 555-0142 or by email at hello@mikurastorage.example. Priya Nair looks after contracts and accounts once a request becomes an agreement. She does not open an agreement for a size that is still full. If you are between two sizes, say so in a visit with Mei Lin Ho rather than joining two lists and hoping. Access hours and key cards apply after you move in, not while you are waiting. The list is only a way to hear about the size you named.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
Contact

The desk is at 48 Alder Row, Lindenport, on 555-0142, from 09:00 to 19:00 every day. Visits are booked ahead and last about twenty minutes with an attendant.

Desk, phone, and email

The desk is at 48 Alder Row, Lindenport, inside the one Mikura Storage building. Phone 555-0142. Email hello@mikurastorage.example. Desk hours are 09:00 to 19:00, seven days. Those are the staffed hours. Daniel Achebe is head attendant in the mornings. Amara Diallo covers the weekend desk, within the same hours. Priya Nair handles contracts and accounts. For a new visit, ask to book a slot. For an agreement you already have, ask for accounts. Building access for people who already hold a key card is 06:00 to 23:00, seven days, and that window is not a promise that the phone will be answered before 09:00 or after 19:00.

Finding the building

There is no map on this page. The direction is the address: 48 Alder Row, Lindenport. Mikura Storage is a dedicated building of six floors, not a counter inside another business. Come to the building and ask at the desk. If you have booked a visit, an attendant is expecting you for about twenty minutes. If you are coming by car to unload, use the covered loading bay and bring the car plate. Rafael Souza looks after the bay and the hand trucks. The hand-truck loan is $0. If you already have a key card, you do not need the desk to be open in order to reach your unit, provided you are inside 06:00 to 23:00. Paint is fresh on the fourth-floor corridors, and that floor is open.

At the desk

  • 555-0142
  • Email the desk
  • Desk 09:00-19:00
  • Key card $0
  • Free loading bay
  • 48 Alder Row

The desk can book a visit, walk you toward a size, and complete a signature. Bring photo ID if you may sign. The first month is paid at signature if you are moving in. Same-day move-in depends on a booking made before 15:00. The visit itself costs nothing and does not oblige you to take a unit. A card is useful only if you decide to pay that first month. Measurements, a list of what you are storing, your phone, and the car plate if you are in the bay are the other things worth having with you. The desk cannot put you into a size that is full. In that case the waitlist takes an email and the size, and no payment.

Before you book

What are the desk hours and the building access hours?

The desk is open from 09:00 to 19:00, seven days a week. Call 555-0142 in that window, or email hello@mikurastorage.example. Staffed means those desk hours. It does not mean an attendant is on duty at dawn or late at night. Building access is wider and unmanned at the edges: 06:00 to 23:00, seven days, by key card. The key card costs $0 and is issued when you move in, not when you merely enquire. Before you hold a card, plan to arrive during desk hours. After you hold one, you can reach your unit inside the access window, including times when the phone is not answered. Both clocks apply at 48 Alder Row only. There is no second building on a different schedule.

How do I book a visit, and what does it cost?

Book a slot on the visit form, or call 555-0142 during desk hours. The form asks for your name, your email, a day, and a size. If you do not yet know the size, say so and the attendant will start from the load you describe. A visit costs $0. It takes about twenty minutes. An attendant walks the corridor with you. You may leave without signing. That is the no-obligation part, and it is literal: no fee is held, because no deposit exists on a visit or on an agreement. If you want a fuller look at the loading bay, say that you are coming by car when you book. Rafael Souza's bay is part of the building, not a separate ticket.

Can I move in on the day of the visit?

Yes, when three conditions are all true. The visit was booked before 15:00. You bring photo ID. You pay the first month when you sign. You then receive a key card, at $0, and you can use a hand truck at $0 in the free loading bay. If the booking was made after 15:00, the desk can still show you the corridor, and move-in waits for a later slot rather than being forced through at the end of the day. If the size you want is full, same-day move-in is not available in that size. Join the waitlist, or look at another size that is actually open. The minimum term, once you have signed, is one month.

What is the minimum term, and how do I end the agreement?

The minimum term is one month. Notice is thirty days. Owen and Lucia Marsh stayed five months, Hana Yilmaz stayed fourteen, and the Okoye family stayed eight. Those longer stays did not use a different rule. They were month by month after the first month, ended with the same thirty days' notice. Give notice to the desk, by phone or email, during the life of the agreement. Priya Nair handles the account side. On the way out, book the loading bay if you need it and borrow a hand truck at $0. The key card access continues only while the agreement does. We do not add a separate cancellation fee in these terms. The notice period is the mechanism.

Which fees are included, and is there a deposit?

The admin fee is $0. The key card is $0. The hand-truck loan is $0. There is no deposit. You pay the monthly price of the size: Shelf $38, Closet $62, Box Room $98, Spare Room $148, or Garage Bay $215. The first of those months is paid when you sign. Optional contents cover is $6 a month if you choose it, on any size, up to $5,000, for fire, water and theft. If you decline the cover, you are not charged the $6. None of the zero fees is a temporary offer with a hidden end date. They are the ordinary terms of the building. A visit before any of this is also $0. You pay when you take a unit, not when you look.

How are the rooms kept, and what does contents cover do?

Rooms are held between 18 and 24 C and kept below 60% relative humidity. Walls are fire-rated. Doors use key cards. The building runs 24-hour video. Jonas Weber carries out building care, including climate and fire checks. These are descriptions of how the building operates. They do not mean that fire, water, or theft cannot affect your goods. Optional contents cover is the separate monthly item for that risk: $6, up to $5,000, for fire, water and theft, on every size. It is optional. Taking it or leaving it does not change the room temperature, the key card, or the monthly rent of the size. If you want the cover, say so when you sign, and Priya Nair adds it to the account.

Book a visit

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
Privacy

This page describes the details Mikura Storage collects at 48 Alder Row, and what the desk uses them for. It is not a certification and it is not a seal.

Who holds your details

Mikura Storage, at 48 Alder Row, Lindenport, holds the details you give the desk. The phone is 555-0142 and the email is hello@mikurastorage.example. Priya Nair handles contracts and accounts, so account questions reach her through that desk. Ines Varga is the founder and building manager. We do not sell lists of households, and we do not pass the visit form or the waitlist form to a separate booking website. Both forms stay with this building. This page says what we collect and why. It does not claim a certification or a seal. If a sentence is not on this page, we are not asking you to assume it.

The visit form

When you book a visit, the form asks for your name, your email, a day, and a size. We use those four items to hold a slot of about twenty minutes with an attendant. If you call 555-0142 instead, the desk writes down the same facts. We do not ask the form for a payment. A visit is free and without obligation. If the day you want is not available, the desk will say so during desk hours, 09:00 to 19:00, seven days. The size you name helps Mei Lin Ho prepare the walk. You may change your mind about the size after you see the corridor. The form is a booking note, not an agreement and not a place on a waitlist.

The waitlist form

When a size is full, the waitlist asks for an email and the size. We use that pair to write to you when a unit of that size is free. We do not ask for a card, a deposit, or photo ID at this step. There is no payment to join. We also do not promise a date, because a full size opens when someone gives thirty days' notice and leaves, not on a clock we can publish. If you would rather look at a different size now, book a visit instead of waiting. You can ask the desk to drop your email from the list by writing to hello@mikurastorage.example or by calling during desk hours.

Photo ID, the agreement, and the key card

Photo ID is required when you sign, including a same-day move-in booked before 15:00. We use it to put the agreement in the right name. The agreement also carries the size, the monthly price, the first month paid, and, if you choose it, contents cover at $6 a month up to $5,000. Priya Nair keeps the account. The key card that opens the door is $0 and is tied to your unit so access works from 06:00 to 23:00, seven days, while the agreement runs. We do not ask for photo ID on a mere visit if you are not signing. We do not ask the waitlist for it either.

Video and the building

The building uses 24-hour video as part of how the doors and corridors are run. It is one of the things every unit includes, along with key-card doors, fire-rated walls, and the climate hold of 18 to 24 C below 60% relative humidity. Video is a building operation, not a household story we publish. We do not put visitors into the stories category. The three stories already on the site, about the Marsh household, Hana Yilmaz, and the Okoye family, are written accounts with names they were willing to have used. Being on camera in a corridor is not the same thing, and it is not consent to appear in News. Questions about a recording go to the desk.

Asking about your own details

Email hello@mikurastorage.example or call 555-0142 between 09:00 and 19:00, seven days, and say what you want corrected or removed from a visit request or a waitlist line. Account records that belong to a current agreement stay for the life of that agreement, because the desk still has to know the size, the price, and the notice period. When the agreement has ended and the thirty days' notice has run, ask Priya Nair what remains on the account and what can be cleared. We will not invent a retention period in years on this page. We also will not ask you to send a copy of photo ID by an open channel if a phone call or a visit to the desk can do the check instead.

pages.title: Terms
pages.content:
Terms

The agreement is one month minimum, with thirty days' notice, at the monthly price of the size you sign for. There is no deposit, and the admin fee and key card are $0.

The agreement

These terms are for a household unit at Mikura Storage, 48 Alder Row, Lindenport. The operator has run this one dedicated building since 2014. An agreement covers one size: Shelf, Closet, Box Room, Spare Room, or Garage Bay. It is formed when you sign at the desk, show photo ID, and pay the first month. A visit is not an agreement. A waitlist email is not an agreement. Until you sign, you owe nothing, because the visit is free and there is no deposit to hold a place. Priya Nair prepares the contract and the account. Ines Varga is the building manager. The phone for the desk is 555-0142 during 09:00 to 19:00, seven days.

Term and notice

The minimum term is one month. Notice to end the agreement is thirty days. A longer stay is allowed and uses the same notice. Five months, eight months, and fourteen months, which are stays households have actually made here, were not special contracts. They were the one-month minimum followed by further months, closed with thirty days' notice. Give notice to the desk by phone or by email at hello@mikurastorage.example. At the end of the notice, clear the unit and return the key card. The loading bay and a hand truck are available for that move at the same $0 loan as on the way in. We do not write a different notice period for a larger size. Garage Bay and Shelf use the same month and the same thirty days.

Price, fees, and deposit

Monthly prices are Shelf $38, Closet $62, Box Room $98, Spare Room $148, and Garage Bay $215. The figures are in US dollars. There is no conversion table on the agreement. The admin fee is $0. The key card is $0. The hand-truck loan is $0. There is no deposit. The first month is paid when you sign. Later months follow the price of the size you took. We do not add a second fee for using the loading bay. If you are unsure of the size, settle it on the visit before you sign, with Mei Lin Ho if you need a size adviser. Signing for a full size is not possible. A full size goes to the waitlist, which takes no payment.

Contents cover

Contents cover is optional. It is $6 a month, on every size, up to $5,000, for fire, water and theft. If you take it, it is part of the account Priya Nair keeps. If you do not take it, you do not pay the $6. The limit is $5,000 even when the unit is a Garage Bay full of a two-bedroom flat. Cover is not a statement that the building is free of risk. Fire-rated walls, 24-hour video, key-card doors, and the climate range are operating conditions of the building. They sit beside the cover. They do not replace it, and the cover does not replace them. Choose it, or decline it, at the desk when you sign.

Move-in and access

Same-day move-in is offered when the visit was booked before 15:00, photo ID is shown, and the first month is paid. You then get the key card and may borrow a hand truck. Building access with the card is 06:00 to 23:00, seven days. Desk hours stay 09:00 to 19:00, seven days, which is when the building is staffed. Do not treat the access window as staffed hours. The card opens the door. It does not summon an attendant after 19:00. Rooms are held between 18 and 24 C and kept below 60% relative humidity for the household goods you store, not as a room to occupy. The unit is storage. The twenty-minute visit is the time we spend with you before you decide.

What these terms do not say

These terms do not include an award or a ranking, and they do not say that goods cannot be damaged or taken. They do not name an insurer, a bank, or any other real brand. They do not set a late-fee percentage, a notice period other than thirty days, or a minimum other than one month. They do not promise a free unit in a size that is full. They do not make the waitlist a reservation. If a corridor is being repainted, as the fourth floor has been, access to the building continues on the key card and the hours above unless the desk has told you otherwise about your own unit. Questions go to 555-0142 or hello@mikurastorage.example during desk hours, and the signed agreement remains the record of your size and your price.

pages.title: Thanks
pages.content:
Thank you

Thank you. The form has reached Mikura Storage, and the desk will take it up during staffed hours.

What happens next

The desk has your form. If you booked a visit, we have your name, email, day, and size, and we will confirm a slot of about twenty minutes during desk hours, 09:00 to 19:00, seven days. If you joined the waitlist, we have your email and the size, and we write when that size has a free unit. We do not promise a clock time for the reply. You can call 555-0142 in desk hours if the day you chose is close. A visit is still free and without obligation. Nothing is charged from this page. When you come, the attendant meets you at 48 Alder Row, Lindenport. You can return to the home page whenever you want to read sizes and prices again.

posts.title: Between two leases
posts.excerpt: Owen and Lucia Marsh kept a studio flat's contents in a Box Room at Mikura Storage for five months while they waited between two leases.
posts.content:
Owen and Lucia Marsh had an emptied flat and a gap between two leases. The cartons were packed. The next set of keys was not ready. They wanted the studio's contents kept together, close enough to fetch, without taking on a second place to live.

They booked a visit at Mikura Storage, 48 Alder Row, Lindenport. A visit here is free, lasts about twenty minutes, and carries no obligation. An attendant met them at the desk and walked the corridor with them. They looked into an open unit instead of choosing a name from a list and hoping. Box Room is 3 m², which is 32 sq ft. On the price list it is the size that fits a studio flat's contents. That was the load sitting with them in the emptied flat: furniture and cartons, not a one-bedroom flat and not a pile that would live in a Closet.

They took the Box Room at the ordinary monthly price of $98. The minimum term is one month. They stayed five. There is no deposit. The admin fee is $0. The key card is $0. They showed photo ID and paid the first month when they signed. The visit had been booked before 15:00, so same-day move-in was open to them, and they used it.

The covered loading bay is free. Rafael Souza looks after the bay and the hand trucks, and the hand-truck loan is $0. They moved the cartons from the hatchback onto a truck and along the corridor. The key card they were given opens the building from 06:00 to 23:00, seven days. Desk hours are shorter. The desk is staffed from 09:00 to 19:00, seven days, and staffed means those hours. After 19:00 the card still works inside the access window. An attendant does not.

The room is held between 18 and 24 C and kept below 60% relative humidity, as the other units are. Walls are fire-rated. Video runs 24 hours. Key-card doors are standard. None of that means the goods cannot be harmed. It is how this one building is run. Optional contents cover is $6 a month, up to $5,000, for fire, water and theft. It applies to a Box Room the same way it applies to any other size. They could take it or leave it at the desk. The $6 does not change the rent of $98.

Five months is long enough for a temporary arrangement to become the place the goods actually live. Owen and Lucia treated the unit as storage, not as a room to visit for its own sake. They left a path between cartons so one box could come out without a full unpack. When the next lease began, they gave thirty days' notice. That notice is the same on every agreement here, whether the stay was the one-month minimum or something longer. They booked the bay again, borrowed the hand truck again, and cleared the Box Room.

The building they used has been here since 2014. It is one dedicated building, six floors, 412 units, five sizes. Ines Varga founded it and still manages it. Their agreement did not depend on a second branch, because there is not one. Priya Nair handles contracts and accounts, so the notice and the last month sat with her. Mei Lin Ho, the size adviser, is who the desk would have brought in if the studio load had been close to a Spare Room. A Spare Room is 5 m², 54 sq ft, at $148 a month, and it is described as a one-bedroom flat. They did not need it. A Closet, at 1.5 m² and $62, would not have taken the studio. The Box Room was the match, and the five months were simply how long the gap between the leases lasted.

If you are in a similar gap, book a slot, walk the twenty minutes, and decide with the door open. Call 555-0142 during desk hours, or use the visit form. Bring photo ID if you might sign, and a card if you might pay the first month the same day. You can also bring a list and the measurements of any piece you are unsure about. If you leave without signing, the visit has still done what it is for.

posts.title: The books came back
posts.excerpt: Hana Yilmaz used a Closet for fourteen months.
posts.content:
Hana Yilmaz used a Closet for fourteen months. A Closet is 1.5 m² (16 sq ft) at $62 a month, described on the price list as a wardrobe's worth and a folded bike. Her load was books. At the end of those fourteen months she shelved them at home again, out of the cartons, which is the moment the piece is named for.

The minimum term is one month, so a stay of fourteen months is simply month following month, with thirty days' notice when the books were ready to leave. Nothing in her stay required a different price or a different building. The Closet was in the same building as every other size: 48 Alder Row, Lindenport, climate-held like the rooms around it. The piece is filed under stories.

posts.title: Room for the cot
posts.excerpt: The Okoye family used a Shelf for eight months.
posts.content:
The Okoye family used a Shelf for eight months. Shelf is the smallest size, 0.8 m² (9 sq ft), priced at $38 a month, and described as ten boxes and a suitcase. In a small bright room at home they folded a cot, and the Shelf took what the room could not. We do not add a first name the family has not given us.

Eight months on a one-month minimum is an ordinary stay, ended with thirty days' notice. The visit before they chose was the same twenty minutes anyone else books, free and without obligation. If a Shelf is full when you need one, the waitlist takes an email and the size. The story is not a claim that a Shelf will always be free on the day you call.

posts.title: Fourth floor reopens
posts.excerpt: The fourth-floor corridors have been repainted, and the floor has reopened.
posts.content:
The fourth-floor corridors have been repainted, and the floor has reopened. This is a note, not a household story. The building has six floors and 412 units. Repainting the corridors does not change the sizes, the monthly prices, the desk hours, or the access window.

Key cards work as before, from 06:00 to 23:00, seven days. The desk remains 09:00 to 19:00, seven days. Jonas Weber continues the building care, including climate and fire checks, across the floors. Rooms stay between 18 and 24 C and below 60% relative humidity. If you store on the fourth floor, you do not need a new agreement because the corridor has fresh paint. The note is here so you are not surprised by the work when you step out of the lift.
